title: Unblock first, then do your own work
detail: On 10/21 two of your four commitments slipped, and one was ECA design feedback David was waiting on. It was still open the next day. Anything a teammate is waiting on goes first.
try: Each morning, before your own list, ask: who is waiting on me? Clear those first. Name them at standup.
source: Simon Sinek, Leaders Eat Last: leaders take care of their people first, so they feel safe to focus on the work.

title: Open the week with the why
detail: Standups are tight and tactical, which is good. Once a week, spend 60 seconds on why this week's work matters to a client: the Olson board on 12/2, a launch, a score that moved.
try: Next Monday, open with one sentence: "This week matters because…", then go around as usual.
source: Simon Sinek, Start With Why: people commit more when they understand the purpose behind the work.

title: Protect the plan from same-day asks
detail: Jamie's SafeTraces work was bumped by a last-minute deck, and Peyton paused David's Verified Inspections design. Interruptions are normal, but right now they land on the team without going through you.
try: Agree with Adam and the strategists: same-day requests for the build team go through you, so you can trade something off visibly instead of it slipping quietly.

title: Make every launch a moment
detail: David's Madison Design Build report had a real number in it (82 to 90). Wins like that and each launch disappear into Asana today.
try: Post a short launch note in team chat for each launch or win: what shipped, one before-and-after number, and who did it. Thirty seconds, every time.

title: One definition of done for launches
detail: Stanwood Camano closed cleanly with a full checklist; other wrap-ups trailed for days (Ride the Tide's last items, Meyer Art Center cleanup). The difference was the checklist.
try: Turn the post-launch checklist into the standard (now without Looker Studio) and run the site audit agent on staging before every launch.

title: Pair every piece of praise with one push
detail: You already notice good work. People grow fastest when they hear both what's working and the one thing to sharpen, said directly and with care.
try: In your next 1:1s, give each person one specific thing that's working and one thing to level up this month.
source: Kim Scott, Radical Candor: care personally and challenge directly.

title: Give Claude Design a home before it spreads
detail: You and David are both moving design into Claude Design (UltraNatural, Verified Inspections), and you flagged that team file organization is chaotic. It's easier to set the structure now than after ten projects.
try: Set one naming and folder pattern (client / project / version) and pin it in the build team chat this week.
